_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); integrated oil and gas signals

pit_profile.why: ExxonMobil: 'Their principal business is energy, involving exploration for, and production of, crude oil and natural gas, manufacture of petroleum products and transportation and sale of crude oil, natural gas and petroleum products'; 'The oil and gas business is fundamentally a commodity business. This means the operations and earnings of the Corporation and its affiliates throughout the world may be significantly affected by changes in oil, gas and petrochemical prices and by changes in margins on gasoline and other refined products'; 'The energy and petrochemical industries are highly competitive'; among the factors it lists, 'the competitiveness of alternative hydrocarbon or other energy sources' and 'laws and regulations related to environmental or energy security matters, including those addressing alternative energy sources and the risks of global climate change' (its own FY2006 10-K): earnings that move with the commodity cycle, by the company's own account; no disruption theme is live for an oil and gas producer, so the alternative-energy and climate-change wording stays here

classification.quality_note: ExxonMobil: 'Their principal business is energy, involving exploration for, and production of, crude oil and natural gas, manufacture of petroleum products and transportation and sale of crude oil, natural gas and petroleum products'; 'The oil and gas business is fundamentally a commodity business. This means the operations and earnings of the Corporation and its affiliates throughout the world may be significantly affected by changes in oil, gas and petrochemical prices and by changes in margins on gasoline and other refined products'; 'The energy and petrochemical industries are highly competitive'; among the factors it lists, 'the competitiveness of alternative hydrocarbon or other energy sources' and 'laws and regulations related to environmental or energy security matters, including those addressing alternative energy sources and the risks of global climate change' (its own FY2006 10-K): earnings that move with the commodity cycle, by the company's own account; no disruption theme is live for an oil and gas producer, so the alternative-energy and climate-change wording stays here. cyclical (obsolescence risk 2/5); price cheap; Ratio B 0.24x; -2% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap +1.73; conservative 2yr +104%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -24.9%/yr (worst year FY97-FY07, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +32.1%/yr (Q4 revenue + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +32.1%/yr (FY97-FY07 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +53.3%/yr (best 2-yr run FY97-FY07); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: XOM (retrospective, 2008-02-01) ◉ BUY — Ratio B 0.24x (51.1% downside to Bear $42 / +216.5% upside to Bull $272) | Adj composite 3.15 vs market 1.42: gap +1.73 [UNDERVALUED] | -2% above the EPP floor $87 (12x FY08E $7.28) | Conservative 2-yr case: +104.2% total (+52.1%/yr) | At 11.8x FY08E the 15% hurdle price $114 sits at or below the BASE case; oil-equivalent production +0.6% in Q4 2007, forward revenues +29.6% (no Q1 2008 revenue guide, Q4 2007 revenue as reported); no disruption theme has dated evidence.
